claims.claimText: Princeton's Generative AI Tools Use Policy (last updated August 2026) governs Princeton administrative and operational information, including student, financial and HR information; it expressly excludes information used for research, academic or instructional purposes. Under it, only University-licensed generative AI tools should be used with University Information classified as Internal or Confidential, publicly available generative AI tools may not be used with such information, and even University-licensed tools should not be used with Restricted information. It is not a blanket rule covering all student coursework or research data.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: The purpose of this policy is to manage the use of Princeton University administrative and operational information with generative AI tools.

claims.claimText: Princeton's Rights, Rules, Responsibilities (2.4) states that generative AI is not a source; where an instructor permits generative AI, students must disclose its use rather than cite or acknowledge it. Disclosure of permitted use is therefore required, not merely recommended, while whether AI may be used at all is set by the course or department. Scholarly Integrity guidance says failure to disclose, even in a course where AI is permitted, is a scholarly integrity violation, and offers a disclosure template.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: Generative AI is not a source as defined in this provision because its output is not created by a person. If generative AI is permitted by the instructor, students must disclose its use rather than cite or acknowledge the use, since it is an algorithm rather than a source.
evidence.snippetLocation: RRR 2.4.7 Generative AI; lines 178-178 of captured page text

claims.claimText: Princeton's Rights, Rules, Responsibilities states that students must adhere to course and departmental generative AI policies, and that inappropriate uses on work submitted for an academic requirement - directly copying output, representing AI output as their own (including rewording or paraphrasing it), exceeding the instructor's parameters, or failing to disclose use (including use for rewording, paraphrasing or editing) - constitute academic integrity violations.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: Students are responsible for adhering to course and departmental policies regarding the use of generative AI. Inappropriate uses of generative AI on any work submitted to fulfill an academic requirement, such as directly copying the output, representing output generated by or derived from generative AI as their own (including rewording or paraphrasing output from generative AI and representing it as their own), exceeding the parameters of use specified by the instructor, or failing to disclose its use (including the use of generative AI for rewording, paraphrasing or editing) constitute violations of academic integrity.
evidence.snippetLocation: RRR 2.4.7 Generative AI; lines 143-143 of captured page text

claims.claimText: Princeton's Dean of the College stated in the Fall 2023 memo that the decision to allow, limit or prohibit generative AI in a course or in undergraduate independent work remains with the faculty. This is consistent with current course-procedure guidance requiring faculty to state their expectations in the syllabus; the 2023 memo is historical context rather than the current governing text.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: First and foremost, the decision to allow, limit, or prohibit generative AI in a course or in undergraduate independent work will remain our faculty’s. Faculty members have the discretion to set their own generative AI policy for their courses.

claims.claimText: Princeton's Office of the Dean of the College requires faculty to set clear expectations for whether, when and how generative AI can be used and to state them in the course syllabus; all students are expected to disclose their generative AI use and not pass off AI-generated content as their own, and faculty may provide their own disclosure template or use the standard one.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: Faculty must set clear expectations for whether, when, and how generative AI can be used and state those expectations in the course syllabus. Work created with the assistance of AI tools should never be a proxy for original work. All students are expected to abide by scholarly integrity expectations for appropriate generative AI use, which include disclosing their use of generative AI and not passing off AI-generated content as their own work.

claims.claimText: Princeton's Rights, Rules, Responsibilities (2.4.5), as quoted by Scholarly Integrity, provides that undergraduates may use only Princeton-authorized academic support: when completing any work to fulfil an academic requirement (homework, problem sets, quizzes or examinations), undergraduates may not use non-Princeton tutoring resources, including AI tutoring bots. This applies to work done for academic requirements; it is not a ban on all AI-assisted study.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: When completing any work to fulfill an academic requirement (such as homework assignments, problem sets, quizzes or examinations of any kind), undergraduate students may not make use of any non-Princeton tutoring resources, including paid or unpaid tutors, independent tutoring services, or AI tutoring bots.

claims.claimText: Princeton's Department of Art and Archaeology prohibits using AI as a text-generation tool in coursework, final examinations and independent projects: students may not submit AI-generated text, use AI-generated text as a draft they then modify or paraphrase, or use generative AI to edit and revise their work. Instructors may grant exceptions for a course assignment with written disclosure, but exceptions will never be made for the junior paper or senior thesis. This department rule is stricter than general course-by-course permission.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: As a result, the Department of Art & Archaeology explicitly prohibits the use of AI as a text-generation tool in the writing of coursework, final examinations, and independent projects alike.
evidence.snippetLocation: Policy on Generative Artificial Intelligence; lines 509-509 of captured page text
